messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: summer workshop: SEM in lavaan
parts:
Hello,

I am teaching a 12-hour introductory SEM course on July 5-7.  It will be taught virtually this year, and I will of course use lavaan for instruction.  As you can read in the course description linked below, the approach is quite practical.  The topics will not be advanced, but they may still be of value to members of this group.  If you have colleagues or students who could benefit from the course, please pass this link on to them.

https://eventum.upf.edu/64915/section/30372/recsm-summer-methods-school-2021.html

There are also several other courses that may be of interest, also in the week prior and following.

Best,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Summer workshops on SEM and Panel Models in lavaan
parts:
Hello,

I am teaching a 12-hour introductory SEM course on July 4-6, as well as an 8-hour introduction to panel models on July 7-8.  It will be taught in person this year, but it is also possible to attend remotely.  They will be taught in the morning in Barcelona, Spain, so the time will unfortunately not be convenient to attend remotely from the Americas or eastern Australia.

I will of course use lavaan for instruction.  As you can read in the course descriptions linked below, the approach is quite practical.  The SEM topics will not be advanced, but they may still be of value to members of this group.  The longitudinal course will include traditional cross-lagged panel models, as well as the random-intercept variety.  If you have colleagues or students who could benefit from the course, please pass this link on to them.

https://www.upf.edu/web/survey/recsm-summer-methods-school-2022

There are also several other courses that may be of interest, also in the week prior and following.

Best,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
